code: # a half-sib design: 12 sires, 2 dams each, 6 offspring per pair nsire <- 12; ndam_per <- 2; noff <- 6 nfound <- nsire + nsire * ndam_per n <- nfound + nsire * ndam_per * noff ped <- data.frame(id = 1:n, sire = NA_integer_, dam = NA_integer_) k <- nfound for (s in 1:nsire) for (j in 1:ndam_per) {   dam <- nsire + ndam_per * (s - 1) + j   for (o in 1:noff) { k <- k + 1; ped$sire[k] <- s; ped$dam[k] <- dam } }  # the tabular method builds A from a pedigree sorted parents-first A <- diag(n) for (i in seq_len(n)) {   s <- ped$sire[i]; d <- ped$dam[i]   if (!is.na(s)) {     A[i, i] <- 1 + 0.5 * A[s, d]     for (j in seq_len(i - 1)) A[i, j] <- A[j, i] <- 0.5 * (A[j, s] + A[j, d])   } } dimnames(A) <- list(as.character(ped$id), as.character(ped$id))  set.seed(9) dat <- data.frame(id = factor(ped$id, levels = ped$id),                   sex = factor(rep(c("f", "m"), length.out = n))) # additive genetic values with sd 1, residual sd 1, so h2 = 0.5 dat$phen <- 5 + 0.4 * (dat$sex == "m") +   as.numeric(t(chol(A)) %*% rnorm(n)) + rnorm(n, 0, 1) fit <- frm(bf(phen ~ sex + (1 | gr(id, cov = A))) + gaussian(),            data = dat, data2 = list(A = A), REML = TRUE,            control = frmtmb_control(check_olre = "ignore")) sd_a <- sqrt(VarCorr(fit)[[1]][1, 1]) c(sd_additive = sd_a, sigma = sigma(fit),   heritability = sd_a^2 / (sd_a^2 + sigma(fit)^2)) #>  sd_additive        sigma heritability  #>    0.9058984    1.0139575    0.4438927

what: Cross-check against the closed-form REML likelihood
title: Case studies: models from the showcase literature
text: gaussian animal model marginal distribution known closed form: y ~ N(X beta, sd_a^2 + sigma^2 ). restricted log likelihood model can written six lines maximized optim(). uses part frmtmb. variance components restricted log likelihood agree six significant digits.
code: X <- model.matrix(~ sex, dat); y <- dat$phen nll <- function(p) {   V <- exp(p[1]) * A + exp(p[2]) * diag(n)   Vi <- solve(V); M <- crossprod(X, Vi) %*% X   b <- solve(M, crossprod(X, Vi) %*% y); r <- y - X %*% b   as.numeric(0.5 * ((n - ncol(X)) * log(2 * pi) + determinant(V)$modulus +                       determinant(M)$modulus + crossprod(r, Vi %*% r))) } op <- optim(c(0, 0), nll, method = "BFGS", control = list(reltol = 1e-13)) out <- rbind(frmtmb = c(sd_a, sigma(fit), as.numeric(logLik(fit))),              closed_form = c(sqrt(exp(op$par)), -op$value)) colnames(out) <- c("sd_additive", "sigma", "restricted_logLik") out #>             sd_additive    sigma restricted_logLik #> frmtmb        0.9058984 1.013958         -300.9229 #> closed_form   0.9058980 1.013958         -300.9229

code: set.seed(31) nid <- 80; nt <- 5 cls <- rbinom(nid, 1, 0.4)              # class membership per subject id <- rep(seq_len(nid), each = nt) dg <- data.frame(id = factor(id), time = rep(0:(nt - 1), nid)) b0 <- 2 + rnorm(nid, 0, 0.5)            # random intercept inside class b1 <- c(0.2, 1.2)[cls + 1]              # slow and fast classes dg$y <- b0[id] + b1[id] * dg$time + rnorm(nid * nt, 0, 0.6) fgmm <- frm(bf(y ~ time + (1 | id)) +               mixture(gaussian(), gaussian(), groups = ~id),             data = dg) rbind(class1 = fixef(fgmm)$mu1, class2 = fixef(fgmm)$mu2) #>        (Intercept)     time #> class1    1.981932 0.227937 #> class2    2.006057 1.258254 pr <- mixture_probs(fgmm) head(round(pr, 3), 3) #>   class1 class2 #> 1      1      0 #> 2      0      1 #> 3      1      0 assigned <- max.col(pr) - 1L # label switching is inherent to a mixture, so score both labelings max(mean(assigned == cls), mean(assigned != cls)) #> [1] 1 dg$class <- factor(assigned[as.integer(dg$id)] + 1L,                    labels = c("class 1", "class 2")) tt <- 0:(nt - 1) b <- rbind(fixef(fgmm)$mu1, fixef(fgmm)$mu2) comp <- data.frame(   time = rep(tt, 2),   yhat = c(b[1, 1] + b[1, 2] * tt, b[2, 1] + b[2, 2] * tt),   class = factor(rep(c("class 1", "class 2"), each = length(tt)))) tinyplot::tinyplot(y ~ time | id, data = dg, facet = ~class, type = "l",                    col = "gray60", legend = FALSE, theme = "clean2",                    xlab = "time", ylab = "y") tinyplot::plt_add(yhat ~ time, data = comp, facet = ~class, type = "l",                   col = "black", lwd = 3) f1 <- frm(bf(y ~ time + (1 | id)) + gaussian(), data = dg) c(one_class = AIC(f1), two_class = AIC(fgmm)) #> one_class two_class  #> 1270.5366  960.2408

M symmetric binary adjacency matrix whose dimnames name locations, gr grouping variable maps observations onto , type one "escar" (proper CAR, default), "icar" alias "esicar" (intrinsic), "bym2" (scaled mixture spatial unstructured part). sd(car) field scale; escar bym2 add mixing parameter (0, 1), reported confint_varcorr() brms’s names car rhocar. intrinsic CAR improper - field identified constant per connected component - icar, esicar bym2 add brms’s soft sum--zero constraint, whose scale con_sd (brms’s 1e-3 default, relative field’s sd). Tightening walks fit onto exactly constrained likelihood; default already four orders standard error sd(car). spde() fits Matern field finite-element mesh: takes mesh’s three matrices (fmesher::fm_fem()’s c0/g1/g2, INLA’s M0/M1/M2) fixed data estimates Q = tau^2 (kappa^4 M0 + 2 kappa^2 M1 + M2). Mesh construction stays outside package. confint_varcorr() reports marginal sd range planar alpha = 2 identities. gr maps observations onto mesh nodes, row number: value gr observation row M0 holds node. finite-element matrices carry dimnames, nothing else can reconcile set labels - label ordering guess, wrong guess permutes field precision still converges. Give gr whole numbers 1..nrow(M0), integer numeric column, character column numbers, factor whose levels numbers; every one spellings model. labeling error. every node observed: node row visits keeps column prior, field still smoothed across . gr one node per observation, mesh place every observation node. general projector matrix, spreads observation vertices triangle falls , supported yet.
code: set.seed(4) grid <- expand.grid(r = 1:5, c = 1:5) nloc <- nrow(grid) W <- matrix(0, nloc, nloc) for (i in seq_len(nloc)) {   for (j in seq_len(nloc)) {     if (abs(grid$r[i] - grid$r[j]) + abs(grid$c[i] - grid$c[j]) == 1) {       W[i, j] <- 1     }   } } dimnames(W) <- list(paste0("L", 1:nloc), paste0("L", 1:nloc)) phi <- 0.7 * as.numeric(scale(grid$r + grid$c)) + 0.7 * rnorm(nloc) dc <- data.frame(loc = factor(rep(rownames(W), each = 8),                               levels = rownames(W))) dc$y <- 1 + phi[as.integer(dc$loc)] + rnorm(nrow(dc), 0, 0.5) fc <- frm(bf(y ~ car(W, gr = loc, type = "escar")), family = gaussian(),           data = dc) confint_varcorr(fc) #>                              block    term type estimate       lwr       upr #> 1 car(W, gr = loc, type = "escar") sd(car)   sd 1.111466 0.8096418 1.5258056 #> 2 car(W, gr = loc, type = "escar")     car prop 0.951133 0.5172424 0.9971797 # node holds the mesh row of each observation, 1..nrow(fem$c0) frm(bf(y ~ x + spde(fmesher::fm_fem(mesh), gr = node)), family = gaussian(),     data = d)

text: Model building four stages. one inspectable output, dry_run = stops pipeline first two. Stage 1, parse. parse_spec() reads formula alone. never touches data. splits linear predictor parametric part (bars special terms removed), list random-effect terms, list smooth terms, special terms mo(), mi(), cs(), gp(), car() spde(). output data free, spec pure description model. Stage 2, assemble. assemble_frame() binds spec data frame produces matrices. parametric part goes stats::model.frame() stats::model.matrix(). resulting terms, xlevels contrasts stored per linear predictor, prediction new data reapplies exactly . frmtmb_control(sparse_x = TRUE) swaps Matrix::sparse.model.matrix(); two paths checked set dropped aliased columns differ. Smooths go mgcv::smoothCon(absorb.cons = TRUE, modCon = 3) mgcv::smooth2random(type = 2). fixed part appended X; wiggly part becomes one-variance block Z, smoothing parameter estimated variance component. Prediction uses mgcv::PredictMat() stored transforms. modCon = 3 makes basis fitted basis: t2() smooth otherwise carries second, sum--zero prediction constraint PredictMat() honors fit . changes fitted quantity. s() t2() supported, te() . Gaussian processes, car() spde() build sparse columns carry auxiliary data (distances, adjacency, finite-element matrices) block. offset() terms summed per linear predictor added eta X %*% beta + Z %*% b. weights() design matrix : addition term multiplies per-observation log density. Every linear predictor’s Z spans whole random-effect coefficient vector, Z column index coefficient index. Columns ordered level major coefficient minor inside block, (level - 1) * dim + offset + coefficient. Terms linked |ID| key merged one block, matter columns land. Stage 3, generate. build_objective() closes assembled matrices returns plain R function parameter list. Family, link covariance dispatch resolve taping, closure stays vectorized free branches parameters. Stage 4, tape optimize. RTMB::MakeADFun() tapes closure random = "b" ("beta" REML), nlminb() moves outer parameters, sdreport() supplies standard errors. can look first two stages without fitting: beta holds coefficients mean linear predictors, betad dpars, b random-effect coefficients, theta covariance smoothing parameters. outer problem four parameters inner problem six.

title: Likelihood-ratio tests between nested frmtmb fits — anova.frmtmb_fit
code: set.seed(1) n <- 200 dd <- data.frame(x = rnorm(n), z = rnorm(n), g = factor(rep(1:20, 10))) u <- cbind(rnorm(20, 0, 0.8), rnorm(20, 0, 0.5)) dd$y <- rnorm(n, 1 + 0.5 * dd$x + u[dd$g, 1] + u[dd$g, 2] * dd$x, 1)  m0 <- frm(bf(y ~ x + (1 | g)) + gaussian(), data = dd) m1 <- frm(bf(y ~ x + z + (1 | g)) + gaussian(), data = dd) anova(m0, m1) #> Likelihood-ratio tests #>  #>                     Df  logLik    AIC  Chisq Chi Df Pr(>Chisq) #> y ~ x + (1 | g)      4 -334.52 677.04                          #> y ~ x + z + (1 | g)  5 -334.05 678.10 0.9394      1     0.3324  # dropping a variance component puts the null on the boundary, so # this p-value is conservative by up to a factor of two m2 <- frm(bf(y ~ x) + gaussian(), data = dd) anova(m2, m0) #> Likelihood-ratio tests #>  #>                 Df  logLik    AIC  Chisq Chi Df Pr(>Chisq)     #> y ~ x            3 -352.75 711.51                              #> y ~ x + (1 | g)  4 -334.52 677.04 36.468      1  1.552e-09 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1  # REML fits compare only when the fixed-effect designs agree, which # is the case for a variance-component test r0 <- frm(bf(y ~ x + (1 | g)) + gaussian(), data = dd, REML = TRUE) r1 <- frm(bf(y ~ x + (x | g)) + gaussian(), data = dd, REML = TRUE) anova(r0, r1) #> Likelihood-ratio tests #>  #>                 Df  logLik    AIC  Chisq Chi Df Pr(>Chisq)     #> y ~ x + (1 | g)  2 -336.69 677.39                              #> y ~ x + (x | g)  4 -325.44 658.87 22.516      2   1.29e-05 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 # differing designs are refused; refit = TRUE compares ML fits instead rz <- frm(bf(y ~ x + z + (1 | g)) + gaussian(), data = dd, REML = TRUE) try(anova(r0, rz)) #> Error : REML likelihoods are comparable only between fits whose fixed-effect designs span the same column space; these do not. Pass refit = TRUE (or refit with REML = FALSE) to compare fixed effects, or hold the fixed effects fixed to compare random-effect structures anova(r0, rz, refit = TRUE) #> anova(): refitting 2 REML models with ML: y ~ x + (1 | g); y ~ x + z + (1 | g) #> Likelihood-ratio tests #>  #>                     Df  logLik    AIC  Chisq Chi Df Pr(>Chisq) #> y ~ x + (1 | g)      4 -334.52 677.04                          #> y ~ x + z + (1 | g)  5 -334.05 678.10 0.9394      1     0.3324

title: Pooled model comparison across imputations (D1, D2, D3) — anova.frmtmb_multiple
text: "D1" Multivariate Wald (Li, Raghunathan Rubin 1991). Let Qbar pooled estimate k coefficients larger model adds, Ubar average within-imputation covariance B -imputation covariance. average relative increase variance r, (1 + 1/m) tr(B Ubar^-1) / k, statistic Qbar' ((1 + r) Ubar)^-1 Qbar / k k v degrees freedom. v uses Reiter (2007) small-sample form dfcom finite Li et al form otherwise. "D2" Pooled test statistics (Li, Meng, Raghunathan Rubin 1991). m per-imputation statistics d - either likelihood-ratio chi-squares (use = "likelihood") Wald chi-squares (use = "wald") - r set (1 + 1/m) var(sqrt(d)), statistic (mean(d)/k - (m + 1)/(m - 1) r) / (1 + r) k k^(-3/m) (m - 1) (1 + 1/r)^2 degrees freedom. D2 needs covariance matrix, cheapest rule least efficient. "D3" Pooled likelihood ratio (Meng Rubin 1992). average deviance difference computed twice: imputation-specific estimates (dbar) pooled estimates (dtilde), second evaluating imputation's likelihood one common parameter vector. r set (m + 1) / (k (m - 1)) (dbar - dtilde), statistic dtilde / (k (1 + r)). D3 default: needs covariance matrix either, unlike D2 stays valid coefficients far normal. Pooled parameter values plain across-imputation means optimizer's parameter vector, variance components pooled internal (log / Cholesky) scale, matching $pooled. model refit: imputation's objective re-evaluated pooled vector, costs one Laplace solve. mice::D3() instead fixes pooled coefficients offset re-estimates every remaining parameter, can differ percent; mitml::testModels(method = "D3") uses plug-form implemented . Note also df.residual() counts dispersion parameter gaussian fit, lm() , dfcom one smaller mice's default; pass dfcom explicitly reproduce mice exactly.

code: set.seed(1) y <- rpois(50, 3)  # a hand-written poisson: check it before fitting anything with it ok <- custom_family(   "my_poisson", dpars = "mu", links = list(mu = "log"),   lpdf = function(y, dpars, aterms) {     y * log(dpars$mu) - dpars$mu - lgamma(y + 1)   },   type = "discrete" ) check_custom_family(ok, y = y, dpars = list(mu = rep(2.5, 50)))  # base matrix() strips the advector class, so the tape sees constants # and the gradient is silently wrong. The check catches it. bad <- custom_family(   "bad", dpars = "mu", links = list(mu = "log"),   lpdf = function(y, dpars, aterms) {     m <- matrix(dpars$mu, ncol = 1)     y * log(m[, 1]) - m[, 1] - lgamma(y + 1)   },   type = "discrete" ) try(check_custom_family(bad, y = y, dpars = list(mu = rep(2.5, 50)))) #> Error : Failed to tape the lpdf: Invalid argument to 'advector' (lost class attribute?). Typical cause: base matrix()/c() stripping the advector class, or branching on parameter values

code: # \donttest{ if (requireNamespace("tmbstan", quietly = TRUE) &&     requireNamespace("rstan", quietly = TRUE)) { # a binary GLMM with small clusters: the regime where the Laplace # approximation and Wald intervals are least reliable set.seed(4) dd <- data.frame(x = rnorm(120), g = factor(rep(1:30, 4))) dd$y <- rbinom(120, 1,                plogis(0.3 + 0.5 * dd$x + rnorm(30, 0, 1)[dd$g])) fit <- frm(bf(y ~ x + (1 | g)) + bernoulli(), data = dd)  cl <- check_laplace(fit, chains = 1, iter = 500, refresh = 0) cl # |z_shift| well above 0 or sd_ratio far from 1 marks the parameters # whose Wald interval to replace with a profile or bootstrap one cl[abs(cl$z_shift) > 0.3 | cl$sd_ratio > 1.3, ] } #> Warning: The largest R-hat is 1.08, indicating chains have not mixed. #> Running the chains for more iterations may help. See #> https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#r-hat #> Warning: Bulk Effective Samples Size (ESS) is too low, indicating posterior means and medians may be unreliable. #> Running the chains for more iterations may help. See #> https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#bulk-ess #> Warning: Tail Effective Samples Size (ESS) is too low, indicating posterior variances and tail quantiles may be unreliable. #> Running the chains for more iterations may help. title: Define a model family — frmtmb_family
text: family Character name family. dpars Character vector distributional parameter names. first entry must "mu". links Named list mapping dpar link name (see frmtmb:::frmtmb_links) link object. lpdf Function (y, dpars, aterms) returning vectorized log-density. dpars named list advector vectors; aterms named list numeric addition-term values (example trials). valid_y Optional function (y, aterms) signals error invalid responses. Called assembly time. init_dpars Optional named list functions (y, aterms) giving response-scale starting value per dpar (applied intercept link). type One "continuous", "discrete", "ordinal", "categorical". last two say modelled response distribution 1..K categories rather number, fitted() returns n x K probability matrix; "ordinal" shares one latent predictor across categories "categorical" gives non-reference category . post Named list numeric helper functions used fitted(), predict() residuals(): mean_fn(dpars, aterms) (response mean), var_fn(dpars, aterms) (pearson residuals) dev_fn(y, dpars, aterms) (unit deviance 2 * (loglik saturated fit - loglik fitted value), residuals(type = "deviance")). family omits one refused method needs . sim Optional numeric simulator (dpars, aterms, n) returning n response draws; used simulate(), posterior_predict() frm_simulate(). stateless rowwise: sees distributional parameters nothing else. family whose extra parameters (extra_pars) enter draw declares fourth argument extra instead. sim_ctx Optional structured simulator (ctx) family whose draws rowwise (see Structured simulators). takes precedence sim. sim_refusal Optional one-sentence reason family simulator, appended refusal entry point raises. Use omission decision rather gap. primary_dpars dpars receive main model formula (default "mu"). Families several location predictors (example multinomial's per-category mu2, mu3, ...) list ; live beta parameter vector integrated REML. lcdf Optional vectorized AD log-safe CDF (q, dpars, aterms) returning probabilities; enables cens() trunc() addition terms. extra_pars Optional function (y, aterms) returning named list numeric starting vectors family-level parameters outside dpar system (example ordinal thresholds). join parameter template names reach lpdf fourth argument. drop_intercept TRUE, intercept column removed main formula's design matrix (ordinal families: thresholds take place).

code: # One-compartment oral pharmacokinetics with between-subject # variability on the absorption and elimination rates. #   dA/dt = -ka A            A(0) = dose #   dC/dt =  ka A / V - ke C C(0) = 0 pk_dyn <- function(t, y, p) {   list(c(-p[1] * y[1], p[1] * y[1] / p[3] - p[2] * y[2])) }  set.seed(2026) tt <- c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12) n_id <- 6 dd <- data.frame(id = factor(rep(seq_len(n_id), each = length(tt))),                  time = rep(tt, n_id), dose = 100) ka <- exp(rnorm(n_id, 0, 0.3))[as.integer(dd$id)] ke <- exp(rnorm(n_id, log(0.2), 0.25))[as.integer(dd$id)] dd$conc <- 100 * ka / (10 * (ka - ke)) *   (exp(-ke * dd$time) - exp(-ka * dd$time)) + rnorm(nrow(dd), 0, 0.3)  if (requireNamespace("RTMBode", quietly = TRUE)) {   # \donttest{   fit <- frm(     bf(conc ~ frm_ode(pk_dyn,                       init   = list(dose, 0),                       times  = time,                       parms  = list(exp(lka), exp(lke), exp(lV)),                       group  = id,                       states = c("depot", "central"),                       output = "central"),        lka ~ 1 + (1 | id), lke ~ 1 + (1 | id), lV ~ 1, nl = TRUE) +       gaussian(),     data = dd, start = list(beta = c(0, log(0.25), log(8))))   fixef(fit)   # }    # Repeated dosing: 100 into the depot every 12 hours. The dose at   # time 0 is the initial condition, the rest are events.   doses <- data.frame(time = c(12, 24, 36), state = "depot",                       value = 100)   frm_ode(pk_dyn, init = list(100, 0), times = c(6, 18, 30, 42),           parms = list(1, 0.2, 10), states = c("depot", "central"),           output = "central", events = doses)    # The same schedule written compactly, and already at steady state   frm_ode(pk_dyn, init = list(0, 0), times = c(6, 18, 30, 42),           parms = list(1, 0.2, 10), states = c("depot", "central"),           output = "central",           events = data.frame(time = 0, state = "depot", value = 100,                               ii = 12, ss = TRUE))    # An elimination rate that doubles after hour 6, carried forward   # from the row it appears on. `tv` values follow `parms`, so this   # dynamics reads ka at p[1], V at p[2] and the time-varying ke at   # p[3].   pk_tv <- function(t, y, p) {     list(c(-p[1] * y[1], p[1] * y[1] / p[2] - p[3] * y[2]))   }   tt <- c(1, 3, 6, 9, 12)   frm_ode(pk_tv, init = list(100, 0), times = tt, parms = list(1, 10),           tv = list(ifelse(tt < 6, 0.2, 0.4)),           states = c("depot", "central"), output = "central") } #> [1] 5.6356414 6.2378071 3.7339432 1.1350284 0.3423811

text: Supported names: "X" Fixed-effect design matrix mu predictor. "Z", "Zt" sparse random-effect design mu predictor transpose. Columns (rows Zt) span whole random-effect coefficient vector, block belonging another distributional parameter contributes zero columns . "beta", "fixef" primary (mu-family) fixed-effect coefficients, named. Coefficients auxiliary distributional parameters separate vector; use fixef() . "b" Conditional modes coefficient space, aligned columns Z. Reduced-rank (rr()) blocks expanded loadings, internal parameter vector. "theta" Covariance parameters internal (unconstrained) scale, confint(). lme4's relative-covariance-factor entries. "lower" Lower bounds theta. internal parameterization unbounded, vector -Inf, lme4's mixture 0 -Inf. Code tests theta == lower detect singular fit never fire; use diagnose() VarCorr() instead. "sigma" Residual standard deviation (sigma.frmtmb_fit()). "flist" grouping factors, one per distinct grouping variable. Smooth Gaussian-process blocks excluded: levels basis functions, groups. "assign" attribute. "n_rtrms", "n_rfacs" Number random-effect terms distinct grouping factors. Multivariate fits one design per response, "X", "Z" "Zt" need resp; names answer without .

code: # two well-separated gaussian components set.seed(3) dd <- data.frame(y = c(rnorm(80, 0, 1), rnorm(80, 5, 1)),                  x = rnorm(160)) fit <- frm(bf(y ~ 1) + mixture(gaussian(), gaussian()), data = dd) # one mu and sigma per component, plus the mixing weight theta1 fixef(fit) #> $mu1 #>  (Intercept)  #> -0.002346141  #>  #> $sigma1 #> (Intercept)  #>  -0.1298411  #>  #> $mu2 #> (Intercept)  #>    4.999987  #>  #> $sigma2 #> (Intercept)  #>  0.01009985  #>  #> $theta1 #> (Intercept)  #> 0.004758874  #>  # posterior class probability per observation head(mixture_probs(fit)) #>         class1       class2 #> [1,] 1.0000000 4.288987e-08 #> [2,] 0.9999990 1.000118e-06 #> [3,] 0.9999851 1.488386e-05 #> [4,] 1.0000000 1.798825e-08 #> [5,] 0.9999891 1.087896e-05 #> [6,] 0.9999952 4.800314e-06  # the mixing weight can take its own predictor frm(bf(y ~ 1, theta1 ~ x) + mixture(gaussian(), gaussian()), data = dd) #> frmtmb fit: y ~ 1  #> Family: mixture(gaussian, gaussian)   Method: ML  #> logLik: -327.164  AIC: 666.328  nobs: 160  #>  #> Fixed effects: #>  mu1: #> (Intercept)  #>   -0.002575  #>  sigma1: #> (Intercept)  #>     -0.1302  #>  mu2: #> (Intercept)  #>           5  #>  sigma2: #> (Intercept)  #>     0.01038  #>  theta1: #> (Intercept)           x  #>     0.01004    -0.07069   # \donttest{ # latent classes: every observation of a group shares one class set.seed(4) n_g <- 40 cls <- rep(c(1, 2), each = n_g / 2) dg <- data.frame(g = factor(rep(seq_len(n_g), each = 5))) dg$y <- rnorm(nrow(dg), c(0, 4)[cls[as.integer(dg$g)]], 1) fg <- frm(bf(y ~ 1) + mixture(gaussian(), gaussian(), groups = ~g),           data = dg) head(mixture_probs(fg))   # one row per group, not per observation #>   class1       class2 #> 1      1 1.262122e-12 #> 2      1 2.820791e-12 #> 3      1 8.436732e-16 #> 4      1 7.884398e-16 #> 5      1 4.031519e-09 #> 6      1 1.439555e-13 # }

code: set.seed(2) n <- 160 dd <- data.frame(x = rnorm(n), g = factor(rep(1:16, 10))) u <- cbind(rnorm(16, 0, 0.8), rnorm(16, 0, 0.8)) e <- rnorm(n)                      # a disturbance both responses see dd$y1 <- 1 + 0.5 * dd$x + u[dd$g, 1] + e + rnorm(n, 0, 0.5) dd$y2 <- 2 - 0.3 * dd$x + u[dd$g, 2] + e + rnorm(n, 0, 0.5)  # each response keeps its own formula and family fit <- frm(mvbf(bf(y1 ~ x), bf(y2 ~ x)) + gaussian(), data = dd) fixef(fit) #> $y1_mu #> (Intercept)           x  #>   1.0775542   0.5517536  #>  #> $y1_sigma #> (Intercept)  #>   0.2721586  #>  #> $y2_mu #> (Intercept)           x  #>   2.0235294  -0.2793594  #>  #> $y2_sigma #> (Intercept)  #>   0.2223223  #>   # rescor estimates the correlation of the residuals fit_rc <- frm(mvbf(bf(y1 ~ x), bf(y2 ~ x), rescor = TRUE) + gaussian(),               data = dd) rescor_matrix(fit_rc) #>           y1        y2 #> y1 1.0000000 0.6720766 #> y2 0.6720766 1.0000000  # set_rescor() turns it on after the fact, and `+` also combines bf()s mvbf(bf(y1 ~ x), bf(y2 ~ x)) + set_rescor(TRUE) #> y1 ~ x #> y2 ~ x #> rescor: TRUE  bf(y1 ~ x) + bf(y2 ~ x) #> y1 ~ x #> y2 ~ x #> rescor: FALSE   # |ID| correlates the random effects of the two responses fit_id <- frm(mvbf(bf(y1 ~ x + (1 | p | g)), bf(y2 ~ x + (1 | p | g))) +                 gaussian(), data = dd) VarCorr(fit_id) #>   y1 1 | g + y2 1 | g [ID]  #>               Name Std.Dev. y1.mu:(Intercept) #>  y1.mu:(Intercept)  0.86060                   #>  y2.mu:(Intercept)  0.61112             0.599

Use allow_new_levels = TRUE to predict them at the population level predict(fit, newdata = nd_new, allow_new_levels = TRUE) #>         1  #> 0.2925272   # a distributional parameter instead of the mean fit2 <- frm(bf(y ~ x, sigma ~ x) + gaussian(), data = dd) head(predict(fit2, dpar = "sigma", type = "response")) #>        1        2        3        4        5        6  #> 1.511247 1.889479 1.426552 2.788566 1.967020 1.432528

code: set.seed(1) dd <- data.frame(x = rnorm(100), z = rnorm(100),                  g = factor(rep(1:10, 10))) dd$y <- rnorm(100, 1 + 0.5 * dd$x + rnorm(10, 0, 0.8)[dd$g], 1)  # `+` combines specifications; the class-wide one goes first so the # coefficient-specific one can override it pr <- set_prior("normal(0, 1)", class = "b") +   set_prior("normal(0, 0.2)", class = "b", coef = "z") +   set_prior("exponential(1)", class = "sd", group = "g") pr #> normal(0, 1) class=b #> normal(0, 0.2) class=b coef=z #> exponential(1) class=sd group=g  # the priors penalize the likelihood: the fit is a MAP estimate fit <- frm(bf(y ~ x + z + (1 | g)) + gaussian(), data = dd, priors = pr) fixef(fit)$mu #> (Intercept)           x           z  #>  1.43922922  0.56382992  0.05323151  # the tight prior on z shrinks it toward zero fixef(frm(bf(y ~ x + z + (1 | g)) + gaussian(), data = dd))$mu #> (Intercept)           x           z  #>  1.43901021  0.57150937  0.06947063   # an empty distribution string sets a hard bound only set_prior("", class = "b", coef = "x", lb = 0) #> (bounds only) class=b coef=x lb=0  # get_prior() shows which rows a design offers get_prior(bf(y ~ x + z + (1 | g)) + gaussian(), data = dd) #>    prior     class    coef group  dpar resp lb ub #> 1 (flat) Intercept                          NA NA #> 2 (flat)         b                          NA NA #> 3 (flat)         b       x                  NA NA #> 4 (flat)         b       z                  NA NA #> 5 (flat) Intercept               sigma      NA NA #> 6 (flat)        sd                          NA NA #> 7 (flat)        sd             g            NA NA #> 8 (flat)     theta                          NA NA #> 9 (flat)     theta theta_1                  NA NA

code: build_objective <- function(frame) {   lps       <- frame$linpreds   blocks    <- frame$re_blocks   block_nll <- lapply(blocks, \(bk) covstruct_registry[[bk$covstruct]]$nll)   fam_lpdf  <- lapply(frame$spec$responses, \(r) r$family$lpdf)   y         <- frame$y    function(pars) {     RTMB::getAll(pars, warn = FALSE)     "[<-" <- RTMB::ADoverload("[<-")     nll <- 0     for (bk in blocks)                       # loop over structure, not obs       nll <- nll - block_nll[[...]](b[bk$b_idx], theta[bk$theta_idx], bk$aux)     dparv <- list()     for (lp in lps) {       eta <- drop(lp$X %*% beta[lp$beta_idx])       if (!is.null(lp$Z))      eta <- eta + drop(lp$Z %*% b[lp$b_idx])       if (!is.null(lp$offset)) eta <- eta + lp$offset       dparv[[lp$key]] <- lp$link$inv(eta)     }     for (r in names(y)) {       yobs <- RTMB::OBS(y[[r]])              # free simulate() and OSA       nll  <- nll - sum(w[[r]] * fam_lpdf[[r]](yobs, dpars_for(r, dparv),                                                frame$spec$responses[[r]]$aterms))     }     nll   } }
